description: Workflow-specific temporal policies whose atoms DO occur in the target workflow's tool/action vocabulary. Authored to exercise PATH-SENSITIVITY: each pair is designed so that a specific pruning strategy (alphabet-only / node-reachability / path-sensitive product) either can or cannot prove the monitor inert. Unlike corpus/policies/temporal_policies.json (generic policies run cross-product against the whole corpus, where most atoms are simply absent), every policy here names an atom that appears in its target, so an alphabet-only check can never prune it -- only a reachability or product argument can. Each policy declares a single 'target' graph (a curated corpus workflow by basename, or a purpose-built synthetic fixture embedded in scripts/pruning_experiment.py).

case_type_legend.response_satisfied: a -> F b where every path that fires the antecedent reaches a DETERMINISTIC consequent node (human / llm step) that dominates all continuations; product proves the monitor never fires. Alphabet-only and node-reachability both KEEP (both atoms present and reachable); only the product prunes.
case_type_legend.response_satisfied_branching: same, on a branching topology (one branch fires the antecedent tool, all such branches reach the consequent).
case_type_legend.bounded_response_branching: a -> F[<=k] b met within k on EVERY branch (deterministic antecedent + deterministic consequent, no conservative tool node in between so the deadline cannot be blown by tool self-refiring). Product prunes; alphabet-only and reachability keep.
case_type_legend.forbidden_unreachable: G !tool:X where X is DECLARED in the graph vocabulary but its emitting node is UNREACHABLE from entry. Alphabet-only KEEPS (X declared); node-reachability and the product both PRUNE (X can never fire).
case_type_legend.forbidden_unreachable_loop: forbidden_unreachable on a looping topology, showing the product proves inertness despite a cycle.
case_type_legend.forbidden_reachable: G !tool:X with X on a REACHABLE node; product finds a bad-prefix witness -> must KEEP (non-vacuous live case).
case_type_legend.response_violated_branch: a -> F b where some branch fires the antecedent but reaches termination without the consequent; product finds an unfulfilled-obligation witness -> must KEEP.
case_type_legend.bounded_too_late: a -> F[<=k] b where some branch reaches the consequent LATER than k; product finds a bad-prefix witness -> must KEEP (shows the bound bites).
case_type_legend.divergent_response: a -> F b on a looping topology where a resolution can postpone the obligation forever; product returns inconclusive (divergent_obligation_possible, infinite runs out of finite-trace scope) -> must KEEP.
case_type_legend.atom_absent_trivial: policy atom absent from the graph vocabulary; ALL static strategies (alphabet, reachability, product) prune -- a baseline sanity pair showing alphabet-only is not vacuously empty.
case_type_legend.uncertified_control: would-be product-safe, but the target fixture carries may-provenance on a traversed edge; the certification gate refuses to emit 'safe' WITHOUT a caller conservatism assertion -> must KEEP. Demonstrates the soundness gate (reviewer fix #6).

policies.motivation: Resume parsing must be followed by human review; on this pipeline the human review node dominates every continuation, so the monitor can never fire.
Interview scheduling must be followed by human review; the review node always follows schedule.
A market-data pull must be followed by human approval; the approver node dominates the pipeline tail.
A Bloomberg data pull must be followed by human approval; the approver node always follows.
Identity verification must be followed by a (risk-assessment) reasoning step; the assessment LLM node always follows on this linear pipeline.
A drop_table tool is declared in the graph but its node is unreachable from entry; the product proves it can never fire, whereas an alphabet-only check would keep the monitor.
On the sensitive branch a PII fetch is always followed by human review; on the normal branch no PII fetch occurs. The product proves the monitor inert on both branches.
After the routing decision a human sign-off occurs within one step on every branch; the product proves the bounded obligation always met.
A retry loop workflow declares an unreachable drop_table node; the product proves the forbidden tool inert despite the cycle.
The trading tool IS reachable; the product finds a bad-prefix witness and the monitor must be kept (non-vacuous live case).
Trades execute as the last tool with no human afterward; the product finds an unfulfilled-obligation witness (must keep).
The approved branch reaches termination after search with no human review; the product finds an unfulfilled-obligation witness (must keep).
drop_table is on a reachable node; product finds a bad-prefix witness (must keep).
A branch fetches PII then terminates via a fast path with no human review; product finds an unfulfilled-obligation witness (must keep).
On the slow branch the human sign-off is two steps after the routing decision, beyond the bound; the product finds a bad-prefix witness (must keep). Shows the bound bites.
A retry loop can postpone the human approval forever; the product returns inconclusive (divergent obligation, out of finite-trace scope) and the monitor must be kept.
A tool-free debate workflow: drop_table is absent from the vocabulary, so ALL static strategies prune. Baseline pair showing alphabet-only pruning is not empty.

Topologically identical to a product-safe response case, but a traversed edge carries may-provenance. Without a caller conservatism assertion the certification gate refuses to prune (inconclusive / uncertified_extraction), even though the run would be safe. Demonstrates the soundness gate refuses to prune uncertified graphs.
